idiom_name: enum Shape with parameterized case classes
implementation_notes: Scala 3's enum covers enumerations and ADTs in one construct: parameterized cases desugar to case classes extending a sealed parent, the compiler generates the companion and the sealed hierarchy, and match over the enum is checked for exhaustiveness. The desugaring is normative, which is why this is the same pattern as the Scala 2 sealed trait form with less boilerplate. Keep the cases in the same file (sealed and enum both require it) and put operations on the enum for behaviour that belongs to the type.
code_sketch:
enum Shape:
  case Circle(radius: Double)
  case Square(side: Double)

def area(shape: Shape): Double = shape match
  case Shape.Circle(r) => math.Pi * r * r
  case Shape.Square(s) => s * s
pitfalls: The type of an enum case constructor application widens to the enum, so a val bound to Shape.Circle(1.0) has type Shape; obtain the case type explicitly when an overload depends on it.
Simple cases of a generic enum are not permitted without an extends clause - a variance or type parameter change can force the Scala 2 style declarations back.
Exhaustiveness still fails silently for values typed as a non-sealed supertype (e.g. Any or a trait the enum extends), so match on the enum type itself.

variants.name: Sealed trait + case classes (Scala 2)
variants.implementation_notes: Scala 2 encodes the sum as a sealed trait with one final case class per variant: sealing restricts all subclasses to the same file, so the compiler can see the whole set and check match coverage, while case classes generate equality, toString, copy and unapply for pattern matching. Nothing is hand-written beyond the declarations, and this is exactly what a Scala 3 enum desugars to; use it on Scala 2 projects or when the variants must also mix in additional traits.
variants.code_sketch:
sealed trait Shape
final case class Circle(radius: Double) extends Shape
final case class Square(side: Double) extends Shape

def area(shape: Shape): Double = shape match {
  case Circle(r) => math.Pi * r * r
  case Square(s) => s * s
}
pitfalls: sealed only constrains direct subclasses: a non-sealed subclass elsewhere can still extend, so keep the hierarchy flat or re-seal intermediate traits.
match on a value whose static type is a supertype of the sealed trait loses exhaustiveness analysis and needs a default branch.
case class copy and equality are structural, so two variants with equal fields are indistinguishable - add distinct fields or a tag when they must be told apart.
